source.title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences

accepted.question_text: In the House Allocation problem, when no popular matching exists, determine whether one can obtain a better approximation algorithm for finding a matching with minimum unpopularity factor or minimum unpopularity margin, or instead prove a tighter inapproximability bound for least unpopular matchings than the currently known negative result for least-unpopularity-factor matching.

evidence.quote: However, future work could explore least unpopular matchings further by finding a better approximation algorithm or proving a tighter inapproximability bound.

accepted.question_text: For Stable Marriage instances with uncertain preferences in the compact-indifference model, determine the computational complexity of SM Probability: given a matching, compute the probability that it is stable when each agent's weak order is refined uniformly at random to a strict preference order.

evidence.quote: 1. PO / SM Probability: What is the probability that a given matching is Pareto optimal / stable?
SM Probability #P-complete ? polynomial
Question marks denote the open cases.

accepted.question_text: For Stable Marriage instances with uncertain preferences in the lottery model, determine the computational complexity of SM HighestProbability: compute a matching with the highest probability of being stable when each agent has a probability distribution over strict preference lists.

evidence.quote: 2. PO / SM HighestProbability: Compute a matching with the highest probability of being Pareto optimal / stable.
SM HighestProbability ? NP-hard NP-hard
Question marks denote the open cases.

accepted.question_text: Beyond Pareto-optimal and stable matchings, study the complexity and algorithmics of fairness notions such as popular matchings and rank-maximal matchings when agents' preferences are uncertain under the lottery, compact-indifference, or related uncertainty models.

evidence.quote: After Pareto optimal and stable matchings, one might consider to investigate other fairness notions under uncertain preferences, such as popular or rank-maximal matchings.

accepted.question_text: For house allocation via exchanges in a social network, determine the complexity and algorithmic structure of the model when exchanges are allowed to occur along cycles of length greater than 2, rather than only through swaps between two applicants.

evidence.quote: The most striking open question regarding exchanges in social networks involves longer cycles instead of swaps only.

accepted.question_text: For house allocation via exchanges in a social network, determine whether natural exchange mechanisms can be made strategyproof, meaning that applicants cannot benefit by misreporting their preferences or strategic behavior during the exchange process.

evidence.quote: Strategyproofness is another topic worthy of investigation.

accepted.question_text: For the NP-hard cases of deciding whether a target matching is reachable from an initial matching, and of finding a Pareto-optimal matching, in house allocation via exchanges in a social network, determine whether these hard cases become tractable under useful parameters and develop a parameterized complexity theory for them.

evidence.quote: Also, the hard cases in Theorems 5 and 6 could be tackled from a parameterised complexity viewpoint.

accepted.question_text: For the Stable Marriage problem, determine the maximum number x_n of stable matchings that any instance of size n can admit, and in particular close the gap between the best known lower and upper bounds for x_n.
accepted.context_brief: Stable marriage; maximum number of stable matchings

evidence.quote: This open problem, first posed by Gusfield and Irving [45], concerns finding the maximum number x_n of stable matchings admitted by any sm instance of size n.
Nevertheless, clearly there remains a large gap between the best known lower and upper bounds for x_n.

accepted.question_text: Given a Stable Marriage instance I and a matching M_0, determine the computational complexity of deciding whether the divorce digraph D_I contains a directed path from the vertex v_{M_0} to a sink vertex, equivalently to some stable matching.

evidence.quote: This leads to a natural open question, namely to resolve the complexity of the following decision problem: given an sm instance I and a matching M0, is there a path in D_I from v_M0 to a sink vertex?

accepted.question_text: For max smti, the problem of finding a maximum-cardinality stable matching in a Stable Marriage instance with ties and incomplete lists, close the gap between the best known lower and upper bounds on the approximation ratio in the unrestricted case.

evidence.quote: These upper and lower bounds for general max smti remain the best known to date, and it is an open problem to close the gap between them.

accepted.question_text: For 1s-max smti, where ties occur on only one side of the market, determine whether the current approximation upper bound can be reduced to 5/4.

evidence.quote: It is thus an open problem as to whether this latter upper bound can be reduced to 5/4 in the case of 1s-max smti.

accepted.question_text: When max smti instances have master lists on one or both sides, determine whether those structural restrictions permit improved approximation algorithms and better upper bounds than are currently known.

evidence.quote: it is an open question as to whether improved upper bounds exist in the presence of master lists on one or both sides.

accepted.question_text: Given an instance I of the Stable Marriage problem with ties, determine whether there exists an efficient output-sensitive algorithm for listing all stable matchings in time O(p(n) + |S_I| q(n)), where p and q are polynomial functions and S_I is the set of stable matchings of I.

evidence.quote: it is an open problem as to whether there is an efficient algorithm for listing all stable matchings, given an instance I of smt of size n. By efficient, we mean that the algorithm should have complexity O(p(n) + |S_I|q(n)), where p and q are polynomial functions.

accepted.question_text: For the Stable Roommates problem, compute p_n, the probability that a uniformly random instance of size n admits a stable matching, and in particular determine the asymptotic behavior of p_n as n becomes large.

evidence.quote: A long-standing open problem, formulated as Problem 8 in Gusfield and Irving [45], is the computation of p_n, the probability that a random instance, chosen uniformly from all possible sr instances of size n, admits a stable matching. Of particular interest is the asymptotic behaviour of p_n, as n grows large.

accepted.question_text: For the general (a, b)-supermatch notion in Stable Marriage or Stable Roommates instances with incomplete lists, determine whether the decision problem “does there exist an (a, b)-supermatch?” belongs to NP.

evidence.quote: However, for the more general case of (a, b)-supermatches, it is not even known whether the problem belongs to NP.

accepted.question_text: For Stable Roommates instances with incomplete lists, determine the approximation complexity of finding a (1, b)-supermatch, or more generally a robust stable matching, that minimizes the repair parameter b.
accepted.context_brief: Robust matchings; approximability of minimizing b

evidence.quote: Genc et al. [41] also provided two metaheuristics for finding a (1, b)-supermatch for a given sri instance that minimises the value of b, however, the approximability of this problem has not been studied theoretically.

accepted.question_text: Develop a theory of robust stable matchings for the Stable Roommates problem, including robustness notions analogous to those studied for Stable Marriage and incomplete-list variants, since robust stability in SR appears not to have been studied in those senses.

evidence.quote: As far as we are aware, robust stable matchings in sr have not been studied previously (either in the senses of Mai and Vazirani [66, 67] or Chen et al. [26]).

accepted.question_text: Improve the current O(N^5) upper bound for computing the weighted straight skeleton of a polygon, possibly by exploiting deeper structural properties of the associated Stable Roommates instance used in the reduction.

evidence.quote: They conjectured that this running time can be improved. A deeper insight into the structure of the underlying sr instance might lead to such an improvement in the efficiency of the algorithm.
